title: What inclusion means
text:
## What inclusion means

**Guidance ID:** IE-FND-001 · **Action owner:** executive sponsor

**Intended outcome:** People can participate, influence decisions and progress with dignity.

Inclusion is the continuing work of making opportunity and participation real. Someone can be employed yet excluded from information, decisions, informal networks, benefits or promotion. Ask what the person can do, influence and access, and what avoidable effort is required. An invitation or supportive intention is not enough.

Accessibility removes barriers in tools, information, environments and processes. Equality concerns rights and fair opportunity; equity recognises that different barriers may require different responses. Belonging is feeling accepted without having to perform a preferred personality. These ideas reinforce one another, but a training certificate or accessibility checklist does not demonstrate them all.

Use autonomy, effort, timeliness, confidence, satisfaction, safety and progression as questions in design and review. A comparable outcome can use a different method. Nobody should have to disclose a diagnosis or mimic colleagues' social style to be respected.

**Boundary:** Do not claim that identical conditions, identical speed or legal conformance alone establish inclusion.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief), [DFW-03](../evidence/source-register.md#dfw-03).
limitations: Do not claim that identical conditions, identical speed or legal conformance alone establish inclusion.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Individuals and intersecting barriers
text:
## Individuals and intersecting barriers

**Guidance ID:** IE-FND-002 · **Action owner:** line manager

**Intended outcome:** Support follows the person and their work rather than a diagnostic stereotype.

Ask what helps with this task in this setting, and what the person wants to try. Disabled, Deaf and neurodivergent identities overlap but are not interchangeable. People with the same diagnosis may have different needs; someone may not identify as disabled or may not have a diagnosis. Ask about identity-first or person-first language when relevant and respect the answer without repeatedly requiring explanation.

Consider fluctuating pain, fatigue, medication effects, time of day, changing environments and temporary barriers. Also consider how race, religion, sex, gender, age, caring, language, income and employment status affect access to support or safety in raising a concern. Do not infer that every difficulty is medical or that situational barriers reproduce every aspect of disability.

Offer a private conversation and an alternative contact if the manager is implicated. If work appears unsustainable, describe the situation and offer support; do not announce that you have detected masking or burnout.

**Boundary:** No diagnosis, strength profile, masking judgement or limitation may be inferred from behaviour or identity.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief).
limitations: No diagnosis, strength profile, masking judgement or limitation may be inferred from behaviour or identity.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Working glossary and shared responsibility
text:
## Working glossary and shared responsibility

**Guidance ID:** IE-FND-003 · **Action owner:** hr

**Intended outcome:** People can use the guidance without specialist vocabulary.

An adjustment is an agreed change to reduce a barrier; a reasonable adjustment has a specific legal context explained in the legal module. Universal provision means an accessible default available without individual negotiation. AAC means augmentative and alternative communication, including typed and device-mediated communication. Assistive technology includes screen readers, magnification, alternative input and other support; it depends on compatible systems and cannot repair every defect.

Job crafting means collaboratively shaping tasks or methods around work outcomes and the person's choices. A workplace passport is an optional confidential record of functional support, not a public profile. Masking describes concealment or suppression of traits or needs; it is not a management assessment category. Psychological safety concerns the ability to raise concerns without fear, rather than a promise that one purchase will eliminate distress.

Managers coordinate action; process, IT, procurement and facilities owners resolve the parts they control. Employees inform choices but do not carry responsibility for making the organisation accessible.

**Boundary:** Employee networks and champions support action; they do not replace accountable owners or legal duties.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief), [DFW-17](../evidence/source-register.md#dfw-17).
limitations: Employee networks and champions support action; they do not replace accountable owners or legal duties.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Specify essential outcomes
text:
## Specify essential outcomes

**Guidance ID:** IE-REC-001 · **Action owner:** hiring manager

**Intended outcome:** Candidates are assessed against work that is genuinely required.

Begin with the purpose of the role, its essential tasks and the evidence that would show someone can perform them with appropriate support. Replace inherited requirements such as “dynamic multitasker”, “confident personality” and “excellent communicator” with the actual task, audience and outcome. A tester might need to document a reproducible fault; that does not automatically require confident public speaking. Do not assume technical jobs have no communication duties.

Describe real location, safety, coverage and collaboration needs and which working patterns can vary. Examine shifts, start/finish times, job shares, remote activities and task allocation even for predominantly on-site work. Do not promise hybrid work that the employer cannot provide or exclude an occupation wholesale.

Publish pay, assessment format, expected duration, tools and an accessible adjustment contact. Review whether qualifications, uninterrupted employment and particular institutions are necessary rather than proxies for capability. Separate equality monitoring from the selection panel.

**Boundary:** Anonymisation can reduce some cues; it does not remove bias from criteria or scoring.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief).
limitations: Anonymisation can reduce some cues; it does not remove bias from criteria or scoring.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Prepare and assess fairly
text:
## Prepare and assess fairly

**Guidance ID:** IE-REC-002 · **Action owner:** hiring manager

**Intended outcome:** Applicants can demonstrate relevant competence through accessible assessment.

Give candidates the criteria, format, practical access details and preparation materials early. As a proposed local default, share interview questions and tasks at least five working days ahead. This is not a statutory period. If unrehearsed performance is essential, document why and design a fair accessible assessment; do not turn test security into a blanket refusal of adjustments.

Offer structured interviews, work samples or paid trials according to the competence being assessed. Avoid unpaid productive work and seek HR advice on trial payment and status. Use the same explicit rubric and equivalent evidence standard across alternative routes. Do not reward eye contact, smiling, fast banter, accent or social similarity. Allow processing time and the approved tools and communication support.

Check the room, quiet, temperature, lighting, routes and remote connection. Supply written directions and, where helpful, images with text descriptions. Invite access requests without asking unnecessary health questions; consult the legal page before pre-offer enquiries.

**Boundary:** Five days and paid-trial design are proposed practice; section 60 health-question restrictions have separate legal authority.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief), [L6](../evidence/source-register.md#l6).
limitations: Five days and paid-trial design are proposed practice; section 60 health-question restrictions have separate legal authority.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Selection boundaries and evidence
text:
## Selection boundaries and evidence

**Guidance ID:** IE-REC-003 · **Action owner:** hr

**Intended outcome:** Selection does not rely on personality conformity or covert profiling.

Proposed policy: do not use personality typologies, personality-fit scores or unsupported trait inferences for selection, performance, task opportunity or promotion. Prefer role-relevant evidence. Do not repeat the claim that every psychometric method is fake science: instrument quality and intended use need specific evaluation. Any proposed cognitive or aptitude test needs documented necessity, validity, accessibility, professional review, adjustment arrangements and a challenge route.

Do not conduct informal screening of candidates' personal social-media accounts. Where lawful role-specific vetting is proposed, require transparent, proportionate, reviewed criteria rather than discretionary searches. Do not infer health, religion or suitability from incidental material.

Optional personality activities can still cause harm. If used socially, participation must be consequence-free; do not retain profiles, label colleagues or quietly use results in future decisions. Do not use AI emotion, facial-expression, personality or disability inference. Tell candidates how relevant assessment evidence is used, retained and challenged.

**Boundary:** These selection restrictions are proposed repository policy, not a claim that every excluded activity is inherently unlawful.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief).
limitations: These selection restrictions are proposed repository policy, not a claim that every excluded activity is inherently unlawful.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Make the first day workable
text:
## Make the first day workable

**Guidance ID:** IE-ONB-001 · **Action owner:** line manager

**Intended outcome:** People begin with usable tools, information and support.

Confirm the start arrangements privately before the person arrives: building access or remote setup, accessible induction, accounts, authentication, equipment, support-worker arrangements and a contact for failures. Test the actual workflow, not just whether a licence has been bought. Supply concise written steps, examples and an accessible induction timetable.

Offer a conversation about communication, focus, breaks, training and working patterns to everyone. A person can discuss a barrier without naming a condition. Agree what the team needs to know about practical arrangements; do not send a diagnosis to colleagues to justify them. Provide accessible routes to HR, benefits, IT and a contact outside the manager.

Set an early check-in and review again after the person has experienced real work. Training may need extra practice time, a sandbox, text instructions or demonstration. Ask which combination helps; a recording or long manual alone may be inadequate. Resolve access before treating incomplete induction as poor engagement.

**Boundary:** Do not wait for a passport, diagnosis or external funding before arranging ordinary practical support.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief).
limitations: Do not wait for a passport, diagnosis or external funding before arranging ordinary practical support.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Use an optional confidential passport
text:
## Use an optional confidential passport

**Guidance ID:** IE-ONB-002 · **Action owner:** hr

**Intended outcome:** Agreed support survives transitions without unnecessary repeated disclosure.

Offer a short passport stating functional barriers, useful arrangements, owners, review triggers and agreed sharing. The employee should be able to check and correct it. Store it only in the employer's approved confidential system, with access limited to roles that need the information. The blank template in this repository must never be completed with real data on GitHub.

At a manager or role change, plan a private handover with the person. Confirm which arrangements continue, which need checking in the new context and who owns implementation. Do not automatically withdraw effective support or require the person to restart every request. Keep the person informed of any proposed changes and supply interim access.

A passport is a support tool, not a waiver of rights or permission to collect a medical history. Portability means useful continuity within agreed boundaries; it does not authorise transfer to another employer or broad access to health information.

**Boundary:** Agreement about practical sharing does not by itself establish a lawful basis for all health-data processing.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief), [L7](../evidence/source-register.md#l7).
limitations: Agreement about practical sharing does not by itself establish a lawful basis for all health-data processing.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: More than one way to contribute
text:
## More than one way to contribute

**Guidance ID:** IE-COM-001 · **Action owner:** meeting organiser

**Intended outcome:** People can contribute without avoidable time pressure or disclosure.

Ask participants what combination of speech, sign, text and advance input works. For AAC users, protect time to complete a contribution and offer an accessible queue or typed route. Do not finish someone's sentences or assume that slow speech means slow thought. A contribution sent before or after a meeting can be as valuable as one made live.

Send the purpose, agenda, materials and decisions needed in advance. A bare “quick chat” request may create avoidable uncertainty; state the topic and whether preparation is needed. Allow a pause or clarification without requiring public explanation. Record actions, owners, dates and decisions in an accessible summary and offer a realistic response window.

Messaging tools can help, but rapid chat can create motor, literacy or attention barriers. Check the actual platform, client, device and task. Keep alternative participation routes and agree response expectations rather than assuming permanent availability.

**Boundary:** No platform or communication mode is accessible for every participant; speed is not a proxy for contribution.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief), [DFW-04](../evidence/source-register.md#dfw-04).
limitations: No platform or communication mode is accessible for every participant; speed is not a proxy for contribution.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Arrange Deaf and hearing access individually
text:
## Arrange Deaf and hearing access individually

**Guidance ID:** IE-COM-002 · **Action owner:** meeting organiser

**Intended outcome:** Participants can follow the full discussion and respond.

Ask about the person's language and communication needs. Not every Deaf person signs, and not every hard-of-hearing person lipreads. Depending on preferences, arrange qualified interpretation, captions, hearing support, text or other provision. Check captions and technical arrangements in practice rather than assuming automatic transcription is accurate enough.

Provide quiet acoustics, good lighting and sightlines; agree seating and interpreter placement. Use one speaker at a time, identify speakers and make remote participants equally able to follow. Do not make the person choose between seeing content and seeing the communication support. Short typed exchanges can help when usable but do not replace full access to a complex discussion.

Respect religious dress, appearance and privacy while arranging an effective communication method. Agree any recording or transcription with appropriate privacy review. Optional sign-language learning can build understanding but is not an interpreter service, and a Deaf colleague must not be required to teach or perform.

**Boundary:** Ask and verify access; do not prescribe a seat, lipreading or signing from hearing status.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief).
limitations: Ask and verify access; do not prescribe a seat, lipreading or signing from hearing status.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Clarity, processing and feedback
text:
## Clarity, processing and feedback

**Guidance ID:** IE-COM-003 · **Action owner:** line manager

**Intended outcome:** People know what is expected and can respond in a usable format.

Agree preferences for text, voice, demonstration, structured notes and check-ins. Give instructions with the goal, priority, action, owner and date, and confirm verbal changes in an accessible written form where helpful. Distinguish required action from background information. Avoid relying on metaphor, hints or institutional knowledge to communicate a concern.

Use consistent names and locations for information; make instructions easy to find again. Break complex work into meaningful milestones and show dependencies. Offer accessible text descriptions alongside visual planning boards. Provide feedback close enough to the event to be useful, with specific examples, a route to improve and time to respond.

Protect time for reflection rather than expecting immediate brainstorming or decisions. Brief predictable check-ins can help if agreed; a compulsory weekly stand-up is not the solution for everyone. Avoid flooding people with repeated notifications or forcing multiple duplicated reporting channels.

**Boundary:** Clear and direct feedback must remain respectful; it does not justify bluntness, infantilisation or unilateral monitoring.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief), [DFW-04](../evidence/source-register.md#dfw-04).
limitations: Clear and direct feedback must remain respectful; it does not justify bluntness, infantilisation or unilateral monitoring.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Use accessible information and shared spaces
text:
## Use accessible information and shared spaces

**Guidance ID:** IE-COM-004 · **Action owner:** process owner

**Intended outcome:** Everyone can obtain the same information and act on it.

Check actual use of email, policies, PDFs, charts, slides, whiteboards and co-working tools. Use meaningful headings and links, logical reading order, readable text and equivalent information beyond colour or images. Provide chart findings and structured data as appropriate. Give text directions alongside maps. Keep alternatives current when information changes.

For a digital whiteboard, check navigation, reading and editing with the team's interaction methods. Agree an alternative way to contribute and receive changes if the board is inaccessible. Do not silently move decisions into an exclusive channel or require someone to depend on a colleague's private interpretation.

Raise defects with the service owner and procurement where a supplier is involved. Check support, authentication and exported documents as well as the main screen. A plain-text summary can provide immediate access while repair continues, but it must preserve decisions, actions and opportunities to contribute.

**Boundary:** A workaround is not closure until the person can complete the intended goal with acceptable privacy and effort.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief), [DFW-06](../evidence/source-register.md#dfw-06), [DFW-08](../evidence/source-register.md#dfw-08), [DFW-09](../evidence/source-register.md#dfw-09), [DFW-14](../evidence/source-register.md#dfw-14).
limitations: A workaround is not closure until the person can complete the intended goal with acceptable privacy and effort.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Work patterns and legitimate outcomes
text:
## Work patterns and legitimate outcomes

**Guidance ID:** IE-WRK-001 · **Action owner:** line manager

**Intended outcome:** Working arrangements support sustainable contribution and real job needs.

Discuss when, where and how tasks can be done, including shifts, start/finish times, breaks, travel, task sequencing and remote activities. Identify actual duties requiring presence or cover instead of treating a job title as a prohibition. Distinguish the statutory flexible-working route from a disability-related adjustment; HR should identify which duties apply.

Assess outputs and impact alongside necessary coverage, collaboration, safety, contracted hours and sustainable effort. Output-only targets can reproduce exclusion if inaccessible tools consume extra time. Consider the whole workload and recovery time. Give advance notice of rotas, software and departmental changes where possible, and a clear route for urgent changes.

Job crafting can change methods or task allocation with the individual, but should not stereotype their strengths, diminish their progression or leave colleagues carrying an unplanned burden. Review effectiveness with everyone affected without sharing private reasons for an adjustment.

**Boundary:** Flexibility is not unlimited and presence requirements are not automatically decisive; assess the particular work and support options.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief), [L2](../evidence/source-register.md#l2).
limitations: Flexibility is not unlimited and presence requirements are not automatically decisive; assess the particular work and support options.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Physical and sensory access
text:
## Physical and sensory access

**Guidance ID:** IE-WRK-002 · **Action owner:** facilities owner

**Intended outcome:** People can use the workplace safely and comfortably enough to do their work.

Review arrival, entrances, toilets, lifts, desk access, lighting, acoustics, temperature, signage and emergency arrangements. Include the remote workstation and travel between work sites where relevant. Ask about the actual task and environment rather than ordering standard equipment from a diagnosis.

Options include a predictable desk, adjustable equipment, reduced glare, alternative lighting, quiet focus zones and headphones. Check whether a proposed solution introduces another barrier: headphones may affect alarms or conversation; voice input may conflict with quiet work; a quiet room may not have suitable access. Seek a combination of space, scheduling and technology that supports all affected people.

Agree a discreet pause or recovery plan in advance, including a safe handover in roles requiring continuous cover. The person should not need a public explanation every time symptoms fluctuate. Provide a usable route for urgent assistance and test emergency access with appropriate safety expertise.

**Boundary:** Equipment and quiet areas are options to evaluate, not guaranteed fixes or substitutes for safe staffing and accessible design.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief).
limitations: Equipment and quiet areas are options to evaluate, not guaranteed fixes or substitutes for safe staffing and accessible design.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Train and change without avoidable disruption
text:
## Train and change without avoidable disruption

**Guidance ID:** IE-WRK-003 · **Action owner:** process owner

**Intended outcome:** People retain access when systems, workplaces or responsibilities change.

Before a change, identify affected tasks, interaction methods and existing adjustments. Explain what will change, when and why; provide accessible training, practice and support. A sandbox, worked example, short text guide or paced demonstration may be more useful than a single large presentation. Allow time for learning without automatically treating it as lower performance.

Test the new version or setup with representative tasks and assistive technology before removing the old route. Plan temporary alternatives and a named escalation contact if launch creates a barrier. Verify authentication, documents and integrations; an accessible main application can still have an inaccessible sign-in or support process.

Review after introduction and at transitions between role, manager and site. Preserve effective arrangements until there is a considered alternative. Record problems and fixes as process learning using synthetic or appropriately anonymised information, not employee medical detail.

**Boundary:** Awareness training alone cannot compensate for inaccessible tools, inadequate time or missing implementation ownership.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief).
limitations: Awareness training alone cannot compensate for inaccessible tools, inadequate time or missing implementation ownership.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Open a practical support conversation
text:
## Open a practical support conversation

**Guidance ID:** IE-ADJ-001 · **Action owner:** line manager

**Intended outcome:** A person can raise a barrier and receive a clear next step.

Accept requests through speech, text or another usable route. A person does not need to use the legal phrase “reasonable adjustment” to start a practical discussion. Ask privately what task is affected, the impact, what helps, what has been tried and what they want to happen next. Do not demand a diagnosis for ordinary support.

Agree what information needs sharing and with whom. Ask whether the current difficulty creates an urgent access, safety, pay or confidentiality issue, and provide interim support promptly. Name the coordinator and date of the next update. If relevant functional advice is needed, explain why and request only proportionate information, using HR or occupational health where helpful.

Use the adjustment workflow and templates to record decisions rather than relying on a conversation that disappears. Keep case information in the approved confidential system. Provide another contact where trust in the manager is low or the manager cannot resolve the issue.

**Boundary:** Practical support need not await diagnosis; legal disability and reasonableness questions still require context and appropriate advice.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief), [L1](../evidence/source-register.md#l1), [L11](../evidence/source-register.md#l11).
limitations: Practical support need not await diagnosis; legal disability and reasonableness questions still require context and appropriate advice.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Decide, implement and review
text:
## Decide, implement and review

**Guidance ID:** IE-ADJ-002 · **Action owner:** hr

**Intended outcome:** An effective adjustment has ownership, implementation and a fair challenge route.

Consider changes to methods, arrangements, tools, environment and support with the person. Involve the owners who can deliver each part. Record the barrier, proposed response, implementation owner, funding, dependencies, interim support and review date. A purchased licence or approved request is not proof of working access.

Test the arrangement in actual work and ask about effort, independence, privacy and sustainability. Reopen the case if it is ineffective or needs change. Review after a change to tasks, manager, location, technology or needs. Do not turn routine review into a recurring demand to prove disability or remove working support without considering consequences.

Where a request cannot be agreed, give an accessible explanation, identify alternatives, retain interim access where possible and explain how to seek a review outside the original decision-maker. Escalate disputed legal reasonableness to HR/legal. Adopt local response targets explicitly; do not invent statutory adjustment deadlines.

**Boundary:** Decisions are individual; neither a catalogue nor a previous employee case settles what is reasonable in another case.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief), [L1](../evidence/source-register.md#l1).
limitations: Decisions are individual; neither a catalogue nor a previous employee case settles what is reasonable in another case.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Separate employer funding from additional support
text:
## Separate employer funding from additional support

**Guidance ID:** IE-ADJ-003 · **Action owner:** hr

**Intended outcome:** Funding processes do not transfer the burden to the employee or delay access.

The employer is responsible for funding adjustments it is legally required to make. Coordinate the appropriate internal budget and escalation rather than making an employee negotiate departmental accounts. Access to Work may support eligible additional needs; it is not a substitute for employer-funded reasonable adjustments. Check current eligibility and agreed costs directly with the scheme.

Provide help with the application where the person wants it, but do not promise a grant, an amount or a reimbursement date. Keep employer action moving while external decisions are pending. Record who will pay, order and maintain equipment and who resolves gaps. Funding information and service availability can change, so recheck before giving specific advice.

Offer relevant coaching, support workers or technology according to the person and task rather than assuming these are necessary for a diagnostic group. Follow the separate Northern Ireland route where applicable; do not silently apply the GB scheme to another jurisdiction.

**Boundary:** Grant eligibility, contribution and reimbursement are scheme decisions; this guide makes no funding guarantee.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief), [L3](../evidence/source-register.md#l3).
limitations: Grant eligibility, contribution and reimbursement are scheme decisions; this guide makes no funding guarantee.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Respond to an inaccessible system or benefit
text:
## Respond to an inaccessible system or benefit

**Guidance ID:** IE-SYS-001 · **Action owner:** service owner

**Intended outcome:** People can use essential services with confidentiality and timely access.

Include payroll, HR, intranet, learning, employee assistance, mental-health support, benefits, collaboration, expenses and authentication in the service inventory. Ask whether people can achieve the real goal, not just open the application. An inaccessible benefit can exclude someone from support offered to colleagues.

Capture the goal, failed step, configuration, interaction method and practical impact with minimum necessary personal information. Reproduce with synthetic data. Put immediate access in place without unnecessarily asking a colleague to handle confidential financial or health information. Give a named owner and update time; do not require the person to prove the defect repeatedly.

Route internal defects to the product or engineering owner, supplier defects through procurement/vendor management, and benefits failures to the commissioning HR owner. Use the system-barrier workflow. Treat a discrimination concern seriously while leaving legal conclusions and remedies to qualified review of the facts.

**Boundary:** Do not assert automatic discrimination, personal liability or supplier breach from the defect alone.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief).
limitations: Do not assert automatic discrimination, personal liability or supplier breach from the defect alone.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Evaluate tasks and cumulative burden
text:
## Evaluate tasks and cumulative burden

**Guidance ID:** IE-SYS-002 · **Action owner:** accessibility lead

**Intended outcome:** Evidence identifies system friction without ranking employees.

Describe the goal, tasks, subtasks, alternatives and recovery routes. Observe representative use with voluntary, accessible participation, alongside what people report. Compare success, errors, steps, effort, fatigue, privacy, independence and time. Account for task familiarity, training, device, configuration and practice effects. Report uncertainty and use repeated observations where practical.

Time differences can reveal a system cost, but no employee should be raced against a colleague or punished for participation. A sighted mouse route is one comparator, not the universally correct standard. Do not import illustrative percentage tolerances from the source methodology as legal or universal acceptance thresholds. Evaluate criticality, frequency and the person's experience.

Estimate repeated burden across the day, including workarounds and recovery, and identify the design changes that would reduce it. Validate repairs against the full goal. A faster workaround that exposes private information or removes independent control is not an equivalent solution.

**Boundary:** The task-analysis method is adapted for employment safeguards; small samples do not establish population differences or individual capacity.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief), [DFW-10](../evidence/source-register.md#dfw-10).
limitations: The task-analysis method is adapted for employment safeguards; small samples do not establish population differences or individual capacity.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Commission and remedy accessible services
text:
## Commission and remedy accessible services

**Guidance ID:** IE-SYS-003 · **Action owner:** procurement owner

**Intended outcome:** Supplier and internal commitments lead to verified fixes.

Before purchase, define representative employee goals, access needs, evidence required, testing, support routes and contract responsibilities. Examine the actual product version and end-to-end workflow rather than accepting a declaration or badge as proof. Include implementation, training, accessible support, updates and exported content.

When a defect appears, preserve a reproducible account, contractual representations and impact. Ask the service owner and supplier for remediation options, dates and verification evidence. Procurement and legal determine relevant contractual remedies, payment decisions and communications; managers must not independently threaten payment refusal or present breach as established fact.

Keep an accessible interim service and monitor it until repair is verified. Include unresolved barriers at renewal and consider alternatives through accountable decision-makers. Prioritise by impact, essentiality, frequency and lack of a usable alternative; do not dismiss a severe barrier because few people have reported it.

**Boundary:** A contract claim is not an employment adjustment; pursue supplier remedies while maintaining access for staff.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief).
limitations: A contract claim is not an employment adjustment; pursue supplier remedies while maintaining access for staff.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Evaluate access before attributing poor performance
text:
## Evaluate access before attributing poor performance

**Guidance ID:** IE-PER-001 · **Action owner:** line manager

**Intended outcome:** Concerns are assessed on fair evidence with access and support in place.

State the work outcome, justified expectation and observable issue. Check whether the instructions, training, workload, tools and agreed adjustments were usable and delivered. Ask privately about barriers and allow the person to respond in a usable format. Separate observed facts from assumptions about motivation, personality or health.

Correct access failures and agree a sustainable plan with specific actions, support, owners and review points. Do not rate eye contact, smiling, speaking speed or participation in optional social activities as competence. Consider work quality and actual role outcomes without ignoring cumulative access effort or necessary recovery.

Investigating barriers does not mean every concern is disability-related or prevent fair action on misconduct. Do not delay action on harassment or immediate safety risks while exploring adjustments. Bring HR into serious or disputed cases and provide an independent challenge route. Keep confidential case records outside this repository.

**Boundary:** This process supports fair judgement and does not determine whether a particular disciplinary decision is lawful.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief).
limitations: This process supports fair judgement and does not determine whether a particular disciplinary decision is lawful.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Absence, recovery and returning to work
text:
## Absence, recovery and returning to work

**Guidance ID:** IE-PER-002 · **Action owner:** hr

**Intended outcome:** Attendance arrangements and return plans account for individual circumstances.

Discuss what absence or medical appointments mean for the work, with appropriate privacy. Consider adjusted trigger points, separate recording or disability leave where relevant, rather than mechanically applying a standard trigger. Agree the approach and explain how records will be used; do not promise that all disability-related absence is automatically excluded.

Plan return with the person, including phased hours or duties, usable equipment, updated training, breaks, coverage and review dates. Check workload rather than compressing a full workload into reduced hours. Explain pay and leave implications through the appropriate HR route, without making unsupported entitlement promises.

Changes may be needed after a short flare-up as well as a long absence. Keep communication predictable and proportionate while the person is away. Before redundancy, redeployment or other consequential decisions, seek appropriate HR/legal review of access, criteria and adjustments rather than treating absence data as a neutral score.

**Boundary:** Absence adjustments are context-specific; the guide does not prescribe unlimited leave, pay or an automatic exemption from review.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief), [L5](../evidence/source-register.md#l5).
limitations: Absence adjustments are context-specific; the guide does not prescribe unlimited leave, pay or an automatic exemption from review.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Make formal procedures accessible
text:
## Make formal procedures accessible

**Guidance ID:** IE-PER-003 · **Action owner:** hr

**Intended outcome:** People can understand, participate in and challenge formal decisions.

Provide clear notice of the issue, relevant material, preparation time and accessible response methods. Agree formats, communication support, breaks and meeting arrangements. Explain the applicable accompaniment rights and consider whether another support person is needed as an adjustment or permitted by policy; these are distinct grounds.

A statutory companion category is not necessarily the limit of support that may be appropriate. Equally, do not promise an unrestricted legal right to any chosen advocate in every meeting. Obtain advice where rights, confidentiality, representation or conflicting roles are disputed. Ensure the person can review the record and raise corrections.

Give an accessible decision with reasons and a route to appeal or independent review. Offer a safe reporting route for bullying, harassment, victimisation or a manager's conduct. Explain limits on confidentiality and avoid retaliation. Urgent safety or safeguarding action should continue through appropriate channels.

**Boundary:** Detailed procedural entitlements depend on meeting type, status and jurisdiction; verify current law and policy.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief), [L12](../evidence/source-register.md#l12).
limitations: Detailed procedural entitlements depend on meeting type, status and jurisdiction; verify current law and policy.

title: Practical awareness and respectful support
text:
## Practical awareness and respectful support

**Guidance ID:** IE-CUL-001 · **Action owner:** line manager

**Intended outcome:** Inclusion is reinforced through everyday behaviour and accessible learning.

Provide accessible, role-specific training in disability, Deaf awareness, neurodivergence, privacy, communication and responding to barriers. Use practical situations and refresh learning through normal work. Do not identify staff as teaching examples or require disclosure. Include paid lived-experience expertise with clear choice over participation and attribution.

Offer peer mentoring and networks without assuming a person wants a mentor with the same diagnosis. Protect time, resources and access. Build a culture where clarification, pauses and differing work methods are normal. Do not tell someone they are masking or insist that visible comfort proves psychological safety.

Sign-language learning or social exercises can be optional shared learning, but do not replace communication access. If an activity excludes a colleague, redesign it with their input or offer an equally valued alternative. Avoid activities that require personal health disclosure or personality labels.

**Boundary:** Training, networks and voluntary inclusion schemes support capability but do not prove compliance or replace operational change.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief), [DFW-17](../evidence/source-register.md#dfw-17).
limitations: Training, networks and voluntary inclusion schemes support capability but do not prove compliance or replace operational change.

title: Make development and progression equitable
text:
## Make development and progression equitable

**Guidance ID:** IE-CUL-002 · **Action owner:** hr

**Intended outcome:** People can grow, earn and lead without having to conform to one career style.

Review access to stretch assignments, learning, mentoring, sponsorship, performance evidence and promotion panels. Publish criteria that reflect the work. Offer technical, specialist and other contribution routes alongside people management where the organisation supports them; do not assume every expert should manage staff to advance.

Check whether flexible or part-time staff miss informal opportunities, whether access failures reduce visible output, and whether disabled colleagues are steered away from ambitious work “for their own good”. Discuss aspirations and support with the person. A spiky skill profile is not a universal neurodivergent characteristic or a reason to confine someone to a narrow role.

Apply the same accessible assessment principles used in recruitment. Include organisational change, redeployment, retirement and exit: use clear information, accessible consultation and a fair review route. Invite voluntary exit feedback without pressuring people to give a diagnosis or attributing every departure to inclusion.

**Boundary:** Career paths must be resourced and published; do not promise a promotion route that has not been adopted.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief).
limitations: Career paths must be resourced and published; do not promise a promotion route that has not been adopted.
warning: Draft exploration only; not approved policy or legal advice.

title: Solve shared problems without exposing a colleague
text:
## Solve shared problems without exposing a colleague

**Guidance ID:** IE-CUL-003 · **Action owner:** line manager

**Intended outcome:** Teams can improve a process while respecting choice and independence.

Ask privately whether the affected person wants team input and what may be shared. Frame the challenge around the process, goal or activity. Explore alternatives, including changes that initially seem unfamiliar, and test whether they work. Do not make the colleague's disability the team-building puzzle.

Buddying can be useful if freely chosen, but check privacy, status, workload and the ability to decline. Keep a route to independent participation; assistance must not become the permanent default because redesign feels inconvenient. Check that the chosen solution does not create a barrier for somebody else.

Document what changed, what was tested and what remained difficult. Share process learning with appropriate permission and without identifiable personal detail. Champions can help spread practical learning with allocated time and leadership backing; owners remain responsible for delivery and resources.

**Boundary:** Permission to try a team solution is not permission to publish a personal story or medical information.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief), [DFW-17](../evidence/source-register.md#dfw-17).
limitations: Permission to try a team solution is not permission to publish a personal story or medical information.

title: Explore optional AI support
text:
## Explore optional AI support

**Guidance ID:** IE-AI-001 · **Action owner:** ai service owner

**Intended outcome:** People can trial useful support with choice, privacy and a workable alternative.

Start with a person-chosen task: organising instructions, drafting a summary, reformatting information or supporting an interaction through an authorised interface. Investigate whether AI reduces the actual barrier and effort. Provide an accessible non-AI route and make declining or stopping the trial consequence-free.

Review the product, actual interface, data flows, retention, security, procurement and permissions. Use synthetic or approved minimum data; do not paste personnel, health or grievance information into an unapproved service. Explain who verifies outputs and how errors are corrected. A simplified document must preserve relevant qualifications and decisions.

Define a bounded trial with the participant: task, expected benefit, success evidence, failure conditions, duration, support contact and rollback. Test accuracy, access, effort, privacy and control. Automatic transcription can misrecognise speech; summaries can omit important action. Record failure as useful evidence and retain support while exploring alternatives.

**Boundary:** AI is an option to evaluate, not a compulsory adjustment or a cure for an inaccessible service.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief), [DFW-08](../evidence/source-register.md#dfw-08).
limitations: AI is an option to evaluate, not a compulsory adjustment or a cure for an inaccessible service.

title: Bound agent actions and employment decisions
text:
## Bound agent actions and employment decisions

**Guidance ID:** IE-AI-002 · **Action owner:** ai service owner

**Intended outcome:** Automation supports people without profiling or deciding their employment outcomes.

Begin with read-only access where appropriate. Grant action permissions only for a defined task with an authorised user, minimum access, clear confirmation points, logging and recovery. Separate drafting from sending, editing from approving, and suggesting from making a consequential decision. Check the interface remains usable with the person's assistive technology.

Repository policy prohibits diagnosis inference, masking detection, personality/emotion scoring, disability-related behaviour monitoring and autonomous hiring, disciplinary, promotion or adjustment-refusal decisions. Human involvement must be meaningful; rubber-stamping a generated ranking is not an adequate governance practice. Check current regulatory guidance before deployment.

Never execute instructions hidden in retrieved documents, emails or applicant material. Retrieve only relevant approved guidance with its qualifications and source. Stop an agent when scope is unclear, access fails, confidential data is exposed or the result cannot be verified. Route decisions to the accountable human owner.

**Boundary:** These are repository governance boundaries, not a claim that every prohibition is a verbatim statutory rule.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief), [L10](../evidence/source-register.md#l10).
limitations: These are repository governance boundaries, not a claim that every prohibition is a verbatim statutory rule.

title: Measure the experience and the response
text:
## Measure the experience and the response

**Guidance ID:** IE-EVA-001 · **Action owner:** knowledge base owner

**Intended outcome:** Improvement reflects actual participation rather than activity counts.

Track adjustment acknowledgement and implementation, whether support works for the person, recurring barriers and unresolved access to essential services. Include independence, effort, errors, fatigue, confidence, satisfaction, belonging, learning and progression. Training completion, scheme membership and equipment purchases describe activity; they do not prove outcomes.

Define each measure's purpose, denominator, time window, missing data and limits before collecting it. Review early retention at relevant intervals, including 12–24 months where useful, but do not infer causation from a departure or assume retention proves inclusion. Lower complaint counts can mean fear or inaccessible reporting; include confidence in raising concerns.

Combine operational evidence with voluntary accessible feedback and appropriately compensated lived-experience participation. Examine recurring process failures and cumulative burden. Give leaders the decisions and resources required, not a league table of people who disclose needs. Validate whether a repair remains effective after change.

**Boundary:** Small samples and self-selection limit conclusions; avoid unsupported causal claims or universal timing tolerances.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief), [DFW-10](../evidence/source-register.md#dfw-10), [DFW-11](../evidence/source-register.md#dfw-11).
limitations: Small samples and self-selection limit conclusions; avoid unsupported causal claims or universal timing tolerances.

title: Collect less and protect meaning
text:
## Collect less and protect meaning

**Guidance ID:** IE-EVA-002 · **Action owner:** privacy owner

**Intended outcome:** Learning does not create intrusive employment or disability profiles.

Separate confidential support records from optional equality monitoring. Determine lawful purpose, necessary data, access controls, retention and relevant health-data conditions before collection. Agreement about a meeting preference does not automatically authorise all health-data processing. Do not infer disability from use of assistive technology or a particular tool.

Use aggregated insights where possible and review small-group suppression and reporting granularity with privacy expertise. Do not publish a universal group-size threshold as law. Participation should not affect opportunities, performance or access to support. Provide accessible information and routes to correct inaccuracies and challenge consequential decisions.

Adapt customer-data methods carefully to the power relationships of employment. Avoid diagnosis-level segmentation without justified need. Never put completed templates, raw research, health records or identifiable grievances in this repository, even if the repository is private. Use approved confidential systems for actual cases.

**Boundary:** The knowledge base provides synthetic structures, not authority or infrastructure to process employee cases.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief), [DFW-07](../evidence/source-register.md#dfw-07), [L7](../evidence/source-register.md#l7).
limitations: The knowledge base provides synthetic structures, not authority or infrastructure to process employee cases.

title: Connect commitments to ownership and review
text:
## Connect commitments to ownership and review

**Guidance ID:** IE-EVA-003 · **Action owner:** executive sponsor

**Intended outcome:** Commitments result in funded action and honest public claims.

Assign an executive sponsor, operational owner and responsible roles for HR, IT, procurement, facilities, privacy and review. Connect commitments to activities, resources, evidence and reporting. Champions enable local capability with protected time and support; they do not absorb every unresolved case.

Review modules annually as proposed local policy, with quarterly checks of legal/funding dependencies and AI guidance and immediate triage after material change or harm. Do not adopt these intervals as legal deadlines. Assess upstream changes before merging them; preserve local qualifications and approval status.

Record conflicting evidence, failed trials and unavailable sources. A maturity method is not certification, and a voluntary scheme is not proof of legal compliance. Keep claims proportionate to evidence. Include disabled, Deaf and neurodivergent people in setting priorities and evaluating results, without forcing representatives to speak for every individual.

**Boundary:** Owners, budgets and approvals must be appointed by the organisation; this draft does not invent them.

**Evidence:** [BRIEF](../evidence/source-register.md#brief), [DFW-11](../evidence/source-register.md#dfw-11), [DFW-12](../evidence/source-register.md#dfw-12), [DFW-16](../evidence/source-register.md#dfw-16), [DFW-17](../evidence/source-register.md#dfw-17).
limitations: Owners, budgets and approvals must be appointed by the organisation; this draft does not invent them.
